title: AI could finally make the super app work in the US. Or kill it for good.
excerpt: Major American tech companies are dusting off their plans to build an app that does everything.
content_html:
The "everything app" is making a comeback.

Invigorated by AI's capabilities, tech companies are again dusting off their plans for building an app that does everything, reports BI's Hugh Langley.

Google and OpenAI recently killed off projects, opting instead to migrate those features into their main offerings. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella even used the term "super app" when describing future plans for Copilot.

So what even is a super app? Imagine having multiple services you regularly use — payments, messaging, social media, etc. — all in one place. China's WeChat is widely considered the gold standard, but the concept is common across Southeast Asia.

Tech giants aren't necessarily looking to replicate WeChat this time around. This type of super app is about consolidating all the AI tools someone might need in one place. The idea is a more seamless workflow that won't require users to work across multiple apps.

Even if it's a new iteration, history hasn't been kind to these types of efforts in the US.

The world's richest man hasn't been able to pull it off. Elon Musk teased plans to turn what was then known as Twitter into a super app called X back in 2023. (At least he got half of it right!)

The X Money debit cards show Musk hasn't given up hope yet. And there's a reason companies are eager to create super apps. As I wrote back in 2023:

"Think about the revenue that type of app would generate. Think about the data that type of app would collect."

So can tech companies finally plant the super app flag in the US?

Super apps success in Asia was largely due to timing. E-commerce took off in the US before it did in Asia. That meant markets like China were more open to super apps than the US, where incumbents were already established and harder to disrupt.

AI's still early, and that might be exactly why this is the moment to try consolidating power as companies get their footing.

Bundling services, in general, has fallen out of favor with US customers over the past decade. Cable TV is bleeding subscribers. People's financial lives are fragmented across multiple apps. We can't even agree on what social media platform to use.

That's also becoming a hot topic in AI. Executives like Alex Karp are touting the need for AI sovereignty to avoid models taking control of companies' data and workflows. A super app is the antithesis of that.

However, the benefits might be too good to pass up.

The tech is perfect for an everything app. It's not just having all the things you use every day in one place. It's an AI that sits across it all, helping you navigate your day-to-day tasks.

And at a time when companies are desperate to show the returns they're getting from investing big in AI, a super app could be the shortcut they need to realize those gains.

Dan DeFrancesco

content_html_zh:
“一切应用程序”正在卷土重来。

商业智能 (BI) 的休·兰利 (Hugh Langley) 报道称，在人工智能能力的推动下，科技公司再次重新制定了开发一款无所不能的应用程序的计划。

谷歌和 OpenAI 最近终止了项目，选择将这些功能迁移到他们的主要产品中。 微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉（Satya Nadella）在描述 Copilot 的未来计划时甚至使用了“超级应用程序”一词。

那么什么是超级应用程序呢？ 想象一下，您经常使用的多种服务（支付、消息传递、社交媒体等）都集中在一处。 中国的微信被广泛认为是黄金标准，但这个概念在东南亚很常见。

这次科技巨头不一定要复制微信。 这种类型的超级应用程序旨在将人们可能需要的所有人工智能工具整合到一个地方。 这个想法是一个更加无缝的工作流程，不需要用户跨多个应用程序工作。

即使这是一个新的迭代，历史对美国的此类努力也并不友善。

世界首富却没能成功。 埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 曾表示，计划在 2023 年将当时的 Twitter 转变为名为 X 的超级应用程序。 （至少他答对了一半！）

X Money 借记卡表明马斯克尚未放弃希望。 公司渴望创建超级应用程序是有原因的。 正如我在 2023 年写的：

“想想这种类型的应用程序会产生的收入。 考虑一下该类型的应用程序将收集的数据。”

那么科技公司最终能否在美国插上超级应用的旗帜呢？

超级应用程序在亚洲的成功很大程度上归功于时机。 电子商务在美国先于亚洲起飞。 这意味着像中国这样的市场对超级应用程序的开放程度比美国更开放，而美国的现有市场已经成熟，更难以被颠覆。

人工智能还处于早期阶段，这可能正是为什么现在是企业站稳脚跟时尝试巩固权力的时刻。

总的来说，过去十年来，捆绑服务已经不再受到美国客户的青睐。 有线电视正在流失订户。 人们的财务生活分散在多个应用程序中。 我们甚至无法就使用哪个社交媒体平台达成一致。

这也成为人工智能领域的热门话题。 像 Alex Karp 这样的高管正在宣扬人工智能主权的必要性，以避免模型控制公司的数据和工作流程。 超级应用程序恰恰相反。

然而，其带来的好处可能太好了，不容错过。

该技术非常适合一切应用程序。 这不仅仅是将您每天使用的所有东西集中在一处。 它是一个无所不在的人工智能，可以帮助您完成日常任务。

当公司迫切希望展示他们从人工智能的大量投资中获得的回报时，超级应用程序可能是他们实现这些收益所需的捷径。
